newsitem.title: CANADA: Oxford Properties shares fall for 2nd day.
newsitem.headline: Oxford Properties shares fall for 2nd day.

text.p: Oxford Properties Group Inc shares slid for a second session on Monday as a broad-based market selloff prompted investors to take profits on the recent high-flying stock, analysts said.

"In this kind of environment, people, where they have profits, are intent on locking them in. There is certainly nothing fundamentally wrong with the company that we are aware of," said Frank Mayer, a real estate analyst with HSBC James Capel Canada.
Oxford was down 1.75 to 21.25 in afternoon trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange. Oxford shares traded as low as 20.30 earlier today.

Shares of the Toronto-based real estate company fell as the benchmark TSE 300 index lost more than one percent of its value this morning. The drop in the TSE 300 mirrored a similar decline in U.S. stocks.

The overall decline in stocks took a harsh toll on Oxford. The real estate company peaked at a 52-week high of 27.50 on February 20 after climbing from 5 on March 29, 1996. Oxford closed as high as 25 last Wednesday.
The company had made no recent announcements and there had been no recent articles that might have prompted the selloff, said Oxford Chief Executive Jon Love.
"There's nothing I'm aware off," said Love.

Oxford's latest announcement came last week, when it said that the Canadian Partners Fund, of which it is co-sponsor and manager, completed the acquisition of phases three and four of the West Metro Corporate Centre in Toronto. The acquisition was a positive for the company, Love said.
Analysts noted that the price of Oxford moved on very low volume in the session. Just more than 6,000 shares changed hands today in Toronto.
